title: Internal site access
description: internal-worker/access.json: who may read internal.blowhorn.ai. .github/scripts/internal_access.py turns it into the Cloudflare Access policy and login methods, and internal-deploy.sh into the Worker's allow list. Only the team's own addresses belong here; other people come from the secret named by extra_emails_env, so they never enter this public repository.

$schema.description: Editor hint: the relative path to this schema. Ignored by the scripts.

hostname.description: The public hostname the Access application protects and the Worker serves. Lower case, no scheme or path.

app_name.description: Display name of the self-hosted Access application in Zero Trust.

policy_name.description: Name of the one reusable allow policy the script manages. Renaming it orphans the existing policy, so change it only with the policy in hand.

session_duration.description: How long one Access login lasts before the person signs in again, in Cloudflare's duration format (for example 24h).

allowed_email_domains.description: Email domains whose every address may sign in (for example layer5.io). Matched exactly: subdomains and look-alike domains are not included. Use an empty list to admit named emails only.

items.description: One lower-case domain name, without @ or a wildcard.

allowed_emails.description: Named addresses that may sign in, in addition to the domains. Repository-listed addresses are public, so keep them to the team's own. Wildcards are not allowed.

items.description: One lower-case email address, with no wildcard.

extra_emails_env.description: Name of the environment variable (a GitHub secret in the workflow) that holds extra addresses, one per line or comma-separated. Its values are never printed and never committed.

allowed_idps.description: Login methods offered on the Access login page, by Cloudflare identity provider type (for example onetimepin for One-time PIN, or google). Each type must match exactly one identity provider on the account.

items.description: A Cloudflare identity provider type, in lower case.
